first.rationale: We face a three-front challenge: competitive pricing pressure on SMBs, declining activation (6% QoQ), and declining onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory_73 shows promotional pricing drove acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMB segments while improving time-to-first-value. This directly addresses the competitive threat while also reducing friction that may be contributing to activation decline. I'm verifying memory_73 to confirm the revenue durability and cross-plan resilience before deploying, and memory_31 to understand whether pricing paired with simplified signup could compound the effect. Memory_86 suggests onboarding simplification also lifted adoption, but given the activation metric is already declining despite prior work, pricing intervention is more likely to move the needle against external competitive pressure. The experiment preserves uncertainty by running at standard scale with clear revenue and activation metrics. Enterprise_sales_assist is valuable (memory_44) but addresses a smaller segment; referral_incentives (memory_57) help existing customers but do nothing for acquisition; activation_messaging (memory_91) has shown value but is a secondary lever when pricing and friction are primary constraints.
